newsitem.title: UK: LIMIT says Janson Green offer unconditional.
newsitem.headline: LIMIT says Janson Green offer unconditional.

text.p: The biggest corporate investor in the Lloyd's of London insurance market, LIMIT, has declared its 18.6 million stg takeover of leading Lloyd's managing agent Janson Green unconditional.

The board of Janson Green, which has this year managed three underwriting syndicates with a capacity of 345 million stg, had recommended the offer to shareholders. LIMIT said on Thursday it had received 100 percent acceptances by the first closing date.

The purchase of Janson Green is one element of a two-pronged strategy by LIMIT (London Insurance Market Investment Trust) to create stronger ties with the Lloyd's businesses it invests in now that the insurance market's recovery plan has succeeded.
Equally, many managing agents are keen to align themselves more closely with corporate capital providers, who have been replacing Lloyd's traditional backers, individuals called Names.

In August, LIMIT said it was poised to buy majority stakes in two large managing agents, the second being Bankside. A LIMIT spokesman said today the Bankside negotiations were "on course", but was unable to comment on when an offer might be made.

Bankside manages eight syndicates with a total capacity of 403 million stg. Capacity is how much business the market can underwrite in terms of premium income. Lloyd's total for this year is 10 billion stg.
LIMIT, which is underwriting 610 million stg, plans to float eventually both managing agents on the London stock market.
